papers.title: OPTIMIZING CLOUD RESOURCE ALLOCATION USING MULTI AGENT DEEP REINFORCEMENT LEARNING-BASED ADAPTIVE HHO ALGORITHM
papers.abstract: Cloud computing workloads are projected to grow by 23.1% annually, with over 80% of enterprises adopting multi-cloud strategies, creating a pressing need for optimal virtual machine (VM) resource allocation to ensure cost efficiency and performance. However, existing allocation strategies suffer from static optimization limitations and inefficient adaptation to dynamic workloads, leading to frequent resource underutilization and service delays. To address these issues, this work proposes a novel Multi-Agent Deep Reinforcement Learning-Based Adaptive Harris Hawks Optimization (MADRL-AHHO) algorithm for cloud resource allocation using the VM Resource Allocation dataset (VM-0 to VM-5 classes). Initially, the dataset is preprocessed through normalization and feature selection to reduce dimensionality and noise. Feature extraction is enhanced using a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) integrated with Firefly Optimization (CNN-FFO), which is benchmarked for learning capacity and solution convergence. However, performance limitations in CNN-FFO under dynamic load conditions are overcome by integrating CNN with Adaptive Harris Hawks Optimization (CNN-AHHO), which dynamically adjusts its exploration and exploitation capabilities based on multi-agent reinforcement feedback. The agents interact with the environment to learn optimal VM allocation policies by maximizing resource utilization and minimizing SLA violations. Experimental results demonstrate that CNN-AHHO outperforms CNN-FFO and traditional machine learning methods in terms of allocation accuracy, convergence rate, and computational efficiency, thereby offering a robust and adaptive solution for cloud infrastructure management.

papers.title: Transformer-Based Scalable Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Joint Resource Optimization in Cloud–Edge–End Video Streaming Systems
papers.abstract: Cloud-edge-end (CEE) collaboration has demonstrated significant potential in video streaming analysis. However, dynamic wireless environments, lack of incentive mechanisms, and constrained resources (e.g., transmission power, bandwidth, and computing resources) remain the primary bottlenecks for achieving efficient CEE-based video processing. To address these challenges, this paper focuses on a multi-user CEE scenario with dynamic wireless channels and investigates the joint optimization of adaptive incentives, cooperative offloading, and resource allocation. We propose a novel framework, called JROC, to motivate edge devices (EDs) to participate in collaborative computation within CEE, thereby enhancing system utility. Specifically, JROC encompasses a smart contract-based adaptive incentive mechanism and an Adaptive Transformer-based multi-agent reinforcement Learning Algorithm (ATLA). The incentive mechanism leverages blockchain to ensure trustworthy and automated incentive distribution, while ATLA captures long-term dependencies and global state features among agents to guide video tasks in dynamic environments through adaptive compression, cooperative offloading, and resource allocation. Moreover, we discuss key steps for deploying the proposed algorithm in a real CEE prototype, including lightweight actor inference at the terminal side and training at the edge. Experimental results based on a real-world operator dataset show that, compared to existing methods, JROC achieves higher long-term system utility while maintaining favorable scalability, thereby validating its effectiveness in resource-constrained and under-incentivized CEE video streaming scenarios.

papers.title: Mobility-Aware Resource Allocation for mmWave IAB Networks: A Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning Approach
papers.abstract: MmWaves have been envisioned as a promising direction to provide Gbps wireless access. However, they are susceptible to high path losses and blockages, which directional antennas can only partially mitigate. That makes mmWave networks coverage-limited, thus requiring dense deployments. Integrated access and backhaul (IAB) architectures have emerged as a cost-effective solution for network densification. Resource allocation in mmWave IAB networks must face big challenges to cope with heavy temporal dynamics, such as intermittent links caused by user mobility and blockages from moving obstacles. This makes it extremely difficult to find optimal and adaptive solutions. In this article, exploiting the distributed structure of the problem, we propose a Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) framework to optimize user throughput via flow routing and link scheduling in mmWave IAB networks characterized by user mobility and link outages generated by moving obstacles. The proposed approach implicitly captures the environment dynamics, coordinates the interference, and manages the buffer levels of IAB relay nodes. We design different MARL components, considering full-duplex and half-duplex IAB-nodes. In addition, we provide a communication and coordination scheme for RL agents in an online training framework, addressing the feasibility issues of practical systems. Numerical results show the effectiveness of the proposed approach.

papers.title: Efficient Resource Allocation for On-Demand Mobile-Edge Cloud Computing
papers.abstract: Mobile-edge cloud computing is a new paradigm to provide cloud computing capabilities at the edge of pervasive radio access networks in close proximity to mobile users. Aiming at provisioning flexible on-demand mobile-edge cloud service, in this paper we propose a comprehensive framework consisting of a resource-efficient computation offloading mechanism for users and a joint communication and computation (JCC) resource allocation mechanism for network operator. Specifically, we first study the resource-efficient computation offloading problem for a user, in order to reduce user's resource occupation by determining its optimal communication and computation resource profile with minimum resource occupation and meanwhile satisfying the QoS constraint. We then tackle the critical problem of user admission control for JCC resource allocation, in order to properly select the set of users for resource demand satisfaction. We show the admission control problem is NP-hard, and hence develop an efficient approximation solution of a low complexity by carefully designing the user ranking criteria and rigourously derive its performance guarantee. To prevent the manipulation that some users may untruthfully report their valuations in acquiring mobile-edge cloud service, we further resort to the powerful tool of critical value approach to design truthful pricing scheme for JCC resource allocation. Extensive performance evaluation demonstrates that the proposed schemes can achieve superior performance for on-demand mobile-edge cloud computing.

literature_themes.theme: Optimizing Resource Allocation in Cloud and Edge Computing Systems
literature_themes.summary: This cluster of papers focuses on advanced methodologies for optimizing resource allocation in cloud-based and mobile-edge computing environments using multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) and other optimization algorithms. The studies propose novel frameworks and algorithms to address challenges such as dynamic workloads, resource underutilization, and the need for efficient computation offloading in video streaming and mobile-edge scenarios.
literature_themes.limitations: The papers highlight limitations such as static optimization strategies that fail to adapt to dynamic conditions, performance issues under varying loads, and the complexity of user admission control in resource allocation. Additionally, there is a need for more comprehensive evaluations of the proposed algorithms in real-world scenarios.
literature_themes.gap_relevance: This cluster identifies significant gaps in existing resource allocation strategies, particularly in adapting to dynamic environments and ensuring efficient user participation in collaborative computing. It supports research gap identification by emphasizing the need for innovative incentive mechanisms and adaptive algorithms that can enhance system performance in cloud-edge computing contexts.

summary: The literature on Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) for dynamic resource allocation in cloud computing highlights innovative frameworks aimed at optimizing resource distribution in both cloud and edge environments. Key studies propose adaptive algorithms to address challenges like dynamic workloads and user mobility, yet they reveal significant limitations in scalability, real-world applicability, and the need for comprehensive evaluations. Gaps in existing methodologies underscore the importance of developing more flexible and efficient resource management strategies that can respond to varying conditions and enhance system performance across diverse applications.
scholarly_positioning: Existing research on Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) for resource allocation in cloud computing primarily focuses on optimizing performance under static conditions, often neglecting the complexities of dynamic workloads and user mobility. While frameworks have been proposed to enhance resource distribution, they frequently fall short in scalability and adaptability, particularly in real-world scenarios where conditions fluctuate. This project aims to address these unresolved tensions by developing a novel MARL framework that incorporates adaptive algorithms capable of responding to dynamic environments and user behavior. By integrating innovative incentive mechanisms and comprehensive evaluations, this research will contribute to a deeper understanding of efficient resource management in cloud-edge computing, ultimately advancing the field beyond current limitations.
research_scope: This study will investigate the application of a novel Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) framework for dynamic resource allocation in cloud-edge computing systems, specifically targeting video streaming services under varying user demands and network conditions. The evaluation period will span six months, during which the framework's performance will be compared to traditional static resource allocation methods and existing adaptive algorithms. Primary outcomes will include system utility, resource utilization efficiency, and response time to dynamic workloads, while secondary outcomes will assess user satisfaction and throughput under different scenarios. The study will utilize real-world data from cloud service providers to ensure practical relevance and scalability of the proposed solutions.
concept_definition: 1. Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL): A machine learning approach where multiple agents learn to make decisions through interactions in an environment, optimizing their strategies based on rewards received from their actions. 2. Dynamic Resource Allocation: The process of distributing computing resources (e.g., CPU, memory) in real-time based on current demand and conditions, rather than using fixed allocations. 3. Cloud-Edge Computing: A computing paradigm that combines cloud resources with edge devices to enhance processing speed and reduce latency for applications like video streaming. 4. System Utility: A measure of the overall performance and effectiveness of a system in achieving its objectives, often quantified as a function of resource utilization and user satisfaction. 5. Resource Utilization Efficiency: The ratio of utilized resources to available resources, indicating how well the system uses its capacity. 6. Response Time: The time taken by the system to respond to user requests or changes in workload, critical for maintaining service quality. 7. User Satisfaction: A qualitative measure reflecting how well the service meets user expectations, often assessed through surveys or feedback mechanisms. 8. Throughput: The amount of data processed by the system in a given time period, important for evaluating performance under varying loads. 9. Adaptive Algorithms: Algorithms that adjust their parameters or strategies in response to changing conditions or inputs, enhancing performance in dynamic environments. 10. Real-World Data: Actual data collected from operational cloud service providers, ensuring that the study's findings are applicable to practical scenarios.
technical_feasibility: The proposed study is technically feasible, requiring access to real-world data from cloud service providers and GPU resources for training MARL models. It does not require open-source model access, hidden state extraction, or labelled datasets, as it focuses on dynamic resource allocation rather than internal model representations. However, if user satisfaction is to be assessed through surveys, a human-subject design and ethics approval will be necessary. The study should ensure that adaptive algorithms are tested in a controlled environment to validate their effectiveness against traditional methods. No significant missing resources are identified, but careful planning for data collection and user feedback mechanisms is essential.
gap: Prior studies have demonstrated the effectiveness of Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) frameworks in optimizing resource allocation in cloud computing environments; however, they treat dynamic workloads and user mobility as fixed or secondary factors, leaving unclear whether adaptive algorithms can significantly enhance performance in real-world scenarios. This matters practically because efficient resource management is critical for maintaining service quality in fluctuating conditions; therefore, this study investigates the integration of adaptive algorithms within a MARL framework specifically for video streaming services under varying user demands and network conditions.
question: How does the integration of adaptive algorithms within a Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning framework impact resource allocation efficiency and user satisfaction in cloud-edge video streaming services compared to traditional static allocation methods under varying user demands and network conditions?
theoretical_mechanism: The proposed research investigates how adaptive algorithms (independent variable) within a Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) framework mediate resource allocation efficiency (dependent variable) in cloud-edge video streaming services. The theoretical framework is based on the premise that adaptive algorithms enhance the system's ability to respond to dynamic workloads and user mobility, thereby improving resource utilization efficiency and response time (system-level outcomes). User satisfaction (user-level outcome) is influenced by the perceived responsiveness of the system, which is mediated by the technical mechanisms of adaptive resource allocation. The causal chain suggests that improved resource allocation leads to higher system utility, which in turn enhances user satisfaction. Assumptions requiring empirical validation include the effectiveness of adaptive algorithms in real-world scenarios and the direct correlation between system performance and user satisfaction.
hypothesis: The integration of adaptive algorithms within a Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning framework will significantly improve resource allocation efficiency (dependent variable) compared to traditional static allocation methods (comparison/control), mediated by enhanced system responsiveness to dynamic workloads, leading to increased user satisfaction.

methodology: This study will employ a Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) framework to optimize dynamic resource allocation in cloud-edge video streaming services. The evaluation will utilize real-world data from cloud service providers over a six-month period, focusing on two primary groups: one utilizing the proposed adaptive MARL algorithm and a control group employing traditional static resource allocation methods. Key operationalized variables include resource allocation efficiency (measured by resource utilization and response time) and user satisfaction (assessed through user surveys). Evaluation metrics will include system utility and throughput, with statistical analyses conducted to compare performance across both groups. Confounding factors such as variability in user demands and network conditions will be controlled through stratified sampling and repeated measures. The study aims for reproducibility by documenting the algorithmic configurations and data processing methods used, ensuring that findings are applicable to similar cloud-edge environments.

proposal: This research proposal aims to develop a novel Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) framework specifically designed for dynamic resource allocation in cloud-edge computing systems, with a focus on video streaming services under fluctuating user demands and network conditions. Existing literature predominantly addresses static resource allocation strategies, which fail to adapt to the complexities of dynamic workloads and user mobility, resulting in suboptimal performance and user dissatisfaction. This study identifies a critical gap in adaptive methodologies that can effectively manage these dynamic conditions, as highlighted by the limitations in scalability and real-world applicability of current frameworks. By integrating adaptive algorithms within the MARL framework, this research posits that enhanced responsiveness to real-time changes will improve resource utilization efficiency and response time, ultimately leading to increased user satisfaction. The theoretical mechanism is grounded in the premise that adaptive algorithms can dynamically adjust resource distribution based on user behavior and network conditions, creating a causal pathway where improved resource allocation directly correlates with higher system utility and user satisfaction. The methodology involves a six-month evaluation comparing the proposed adaptive MARL algorithm against traditional static allocation methods, utilizing real-world data from cloud service providers. Key operationalized constructs include algorithm performance metrics (adaptability score, response time), resource allocation efficiency (measured through resource utilization rates and system response times), and user satisfaction (assessed via structured user surveys). Statistical analyses will be employed to ensure robust evaluation, controlling for confounding factors such as variability in user demands and network conditions through stratified sampling. Expected contributions encompass theoretical advancements in adaptive resource allocation, the development of a tailored MARL algorithm, empirical insights from real-world evaluations, and practical deployment guidelines for cloud service providers. Potential limitations, such as data sparsity and low user engagement, will be addressed through targeted mitigation strategies, ensuring the feasibility and relevance of the proposed research.
